question: Show that the function $f: \mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{Z}$ defined by $f(x) = -x$ is one-one and onto.
explanation:
To show one-one, suppose $f(x_1)=f(x_2)$.

Then $-x_1=-x_2$ which implies $x_1=x_2$. Hence $f$ is one-one.

To show onto, take any $y \in \mathbb{Z}$.

Let $x=-y$. Then $f(x)=-(-y)=y$.

Thus every integer has a preimage and the function is onto.

Hence $f(x)=-x$ is bijective.
